# Mitochondria Localized microRNAs: An Unexplored miRNA Niche in Alzheimer’s Disease and Aging

**Авторы:** Rivera Jazmin, Gangwani Laxman, Kumar Subodh

**Журнал:** Cells (2023)
source_units.reason: article_metadata_header

source_units.text:
**DOI:** 10.3390/cells12050742


## Abstract
source_units.reason: bibliographic_metadata

source_units.text: Mitochondria play several vital roles in the brain cells, especially in neurons to provide synaptic energy (ATP), Ca2+ homeostasis, Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) production, apoptosis, mitophagy, axonal transport and neurotransmission.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a well-established phenomenon in the pathophysiology of many neurological diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Amyloid-beta (Aβ) and Phosphorylated tau (p-tau) proteins cause the severe mitochondrial defects in AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A newly discovered cellular niche of microRNAs (miRNAs), so-called mitochondrial-miRNAs (mito-miRs), has recently been explored in mitochondrial functions, cellular processes and in a few human diseases.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The mitochondria localized miRNAs regulate local mitochondrial genes expression and are significantly involved in the modulation of mitochondrial proteins, and thereby in controlling mitochondrial function.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Thus, mitochondrial miRNAs are crucial to maintaining mitochondrial integrity and for normal mitochondrial homeostasis.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Mitochondrial dysfunction is well established in AD pathogenesis, but unfortunately mitochondria miRNAs and their precise roles have not yet been investigated in AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Therefore, an urgent need exists to examine and decipher the critical roles of mitochondrial miRNAs in AD and in the aging process.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The current perspective sheds light on the latest insights and future research directions on investigating the contribution of mitochondrial miRNAs in AD and aging.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
Alzheimer’s Disease

Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurological disorder that affects approximately 50 million people worldwide [1].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Alzheimer’s disease is ranked as the seventh leading cause of death in the United States and is most associated with dementia among older adults (https://www.nia.nih.gov/health/alzheimers-disease-fact-sheet, accessed on 15 October 2022).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Dementia refers to a loss of cognitive function, with a broad range of symptoms depending on the stage of diagnosis.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Memory loss, an inability to carry out daily activities and a difficulty in organizing thoughts and thinking logically are symptoms associated with brain atrophy caused by AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: Researchers continue to unravel complex changes involving the AD brain.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Alzheimer’s has been divided into familial and sporadic forms associated with the stages of the disease.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: According to studies, early-onset (familial) cases account for ~10% of all patients with AD, primarily affected individuals below 65 years of age.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: On the other hand, late-onset (sporadic) contributes up to 30% of all patients with AD developing before the age of 65 [2].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Certain AD cases are caused by inherited changes within genes.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Early-onset AD has been linked to mutations on chromosome 19, entailing the apolipoprotein E (APOE) gene.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, a large body of research suggests that other genetic components may also be involved in the manifestation of AD, such as mutations in amyloid-beta precursor protein (AβPP), presenilin1, and presenilin 2 genes attributing to the overproduction of Aβ plaques.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A group of proteins and peptides including transthyretin, calcitonin, gelsolin, amylin, atrial natriuretic peptide and amyloid-beta have been hallmarked as the fibrillar components of diseases that are characterized by amyloid deposits [2].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: We recently conducted a meta-analysis study on the deregulated mitochondrial microRNAs (miRNAs) in AD [3].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: We reviewed and proposed the potential roles of mitochondrial miRNAs in mitochondrial activities and synapse function.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, our meta-analysis study lacked information about brain mitochondria localized miRNAs and their relevance in AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The main objective of the current article is to unveil the mitochondria localized and associated miRNAs and their critical role in maintaining the normal mitochondrial function and in AD pathogenesis.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
Mitochondria and Alzheimer’s Disease

The mitochondrion is an important cellular component known for its role in bioenergetics, metabolism, signaling pathways and cell viability [4].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Mitochondria play several vital roles in the brain cells, especially in neurons to provide synaptic energy (ATP), Ca2+ handling, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, apoptosis, mitophagy, axonal transport and neurotransmission [5,6,7].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: It is established that a healthy pool of mitochondria provides necessary energy to the neurons for proper neuronal function and synaptic activity.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The mitochondria also protect neurons from oxidative stress and free radical damages [5,6,7].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: It is reported that mitochondrial dysfunction is a new hallmark of AD initiation and progression [8,9,10].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A number of mitochondrial abnormalities are reported in the AD brain, including disrupted mitochondrial bioenergetics, increased oxidative stress, mitochondrial genomic stress, abnormal mitochondrial fusion and fission, mitochondrial axonal trafficking deficits and abnormal mitochondrial distribution, impaired mitochondrial biogenesis, abnormal endoplasmic reticulum–mitochondrial interaction, impaired mitophagy and impaired mitochondrial proteostasis [5,6,7,8].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: All these mitochondrial dysfunctions are caused by multiple biological, genetic, and environmental factors, including Aging, Aβ and p-tau toxicities, inflammation, miRNAs deregulation, gender differences and environmental toxins [3,8,9,10,11].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Mitochondrial dysfunction has a significant negative impact on synaptic activities in AD, such as impaired calcium signaling, reduced synaptic energy, defective neurotransmission, and synaptic dysfunction [5,6,7,8,9,10,11].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: As mitochondrial genome disturbance is one of the contributing factors for mitochondrial dysfunction in AD, it is important to uncover the mitochondrial genome-associated miRNAs deregulation and their impact on mitochondrial and synaptic dysfunction in AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: MicroRNAs
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are regulators of human genes, and their therapeutic relevance has been explored in human diseases, including AD [3].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: MiRNAs are present throughout the cells and some miRNAs are localized to cellular organelles.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Subcellular compartmentalization and localization of miRNAs, miRNA-induced silencing complex (miRISC) and target mRNA have been observed to localize in multiple subcellular compartments including mitochondria, nucleus, rough endoplasmic reticulum, processing (P)-bodies, early/late endosomes, multivesicular bodies, lysosomes and synaptosomes [3,12,13,14,15,16,17].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: MiRNAs are small and noncoding RNAs that regulate gene expression through the process of binding to messenger RNA (mRNA) [3,16,17,18].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: According to studies, miRNAs are attributed to the post-transcriptional regulation of mitochondrial gene expression and control mitochondrial activities [19].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: MiRNAs are transcribed as double-stranded RNA, also known as pre-miRNA.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: On the other hand, mature miRNAs bind to Argonaute proteins that form the RNA-induced silencing complex ribonucleoprotein (RISC) [4].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Pre-miRNAs and mature miRNAs found in the mitochondria interfere with mitochondrial genome derived mRNA, which affects the mitochondria and cell function.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Through complementary base pairing RISC binds to 3’-UTR, thus downregulating gene expression.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The result of this process initiates mRNA degradation or translational repression affecting the production of protein levels [3,20].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: MiRNAs found in the central nervous system play a role in the translation and degradation of genes.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: According to recent research, synaptic activity and function has been linked to miRNAs due to their ability to interact with mRNAs, resulting in physiological changes [16].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: # 4. MiRNAs Localization in Mitochondria
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Specific mitochondrial miRNAs are miRNAs that are localized in the mitochondria.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The presence of miRNA in mitochondria has only been discovered in the past decade in living organisms.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Several studies have identified the presence of miRNAs in the mitochondria and their important roles in local mitochondrial protein synthesis, and in the regulation of mitochondrial functions [12,13,14,17].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Initially, in 2009, Kren et al., identified the rat-liver-derived mitochondrial miRNAs and unveiled their roles in apoptosis [12].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The five miRNAs—miR-130a, miR-130b, miR-140, miR-320 and miR-494—were identified as mitochondrial enriched miRNAs, and most of them are involved in the expression of genes associated with apoptosis, cell proliferation, and differentiation [12].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In 2011, Barrey et al. studied the miRNA localized in the mitochondria isolated from human skeletal primary muscular cells [17].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The three precursor miRNAs—pre-mir-302a, pre-let-7b and mir-365—were found to be localized in the mitochondria of human myoblasts [17].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In the same year, Bendiera et al. studied mitochondrial-enriched miRNAs in HeLa cells [14].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: First, the author separated the mitochondrial and cytosolic fraction from the same samples of HeLa cells.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Next, they performed the miRNAs analysis in both mitochondria and cytosolic fraction.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A total of 57 miRNAs was found to be significantly deregulated in the mitochondria versus the cytosol.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The three nuclear-encoded miRNAs signatures hsa-miR-494, hsa-miR-1275 and hsa-miR-1974 were found to be consistently upregulated in mitochondria [14].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Further, the author found the presence of Argonaute 2 protein in the mitochondria, which suggests that mitochondria miRNAs could modulate the expression of local mitochondrial proteins [14].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Therefore, the precise roles and therapeutic relevance of these mitochondria localized miRNAs are still unknown.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Hence, despite all information and available research [3,20,21,22,23,24,25], mitochondrial miRNAs are still an unexplored niche in human diseases [22], neurological disorders.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
Mitochondria Localized miRNAs and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in AD

Alzheimer’s disease is tied to mitochondrial dysfunction, including overproduction of ROS, low ATP production and influx of calcium ion.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The disruption of calcium homeostasis causes damage to the mitochondria, resulting in damage to synaptic dysfunction.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Together, all these features contribute to the dysfunction of the mitochondria, leading to the progression of AD [2].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Furthermore, Aβ plaques and NFTs have been associated with impeding mitochondrial function increasing neuronal deficits, leading to neurodegeneration associated with neurological disorders such as AD [26].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Mitochondrial respiration defects are the characteristics found in the brains of patient with AD. Decreased neurological function, impairments and brain atrophy have been tied to the reduction in mitochondrial enzyme activity in the premorbid cognitive level [18].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: MiR-338 is a brain-specific miRNA that has been shown to modulate the expression of cytochrome c oxidase IV (COXIV), a protein within the ETC which contributes to ATP production, in neuronal cells [27].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Moreover, the expression of miR-338 is correlated to the reduction in COXIV mRNA and reduction in protein levels.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A study based on the control of mitochondrial activity by miRNAs revealed overexpression of miR-338 reduced mitochondrial oxygen consumption, metabolic activity, and ATP production [21].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: MiRNAs mediated mitochondrial impairment decreases ATP production, alters calcium influx, and increases ROS production.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A decrease in ROS concentration is essential for normal cell signaling; on the other hand, a high concentration of ROS damages macromolecules and increases the mutation rate of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Studies have linked mitochondrial dysfunction with age and oxidative stress, contributing to neurodegenerative diseases [18].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Furthermore, quite a few specific miRNAs play important roles in mitochondrial function, as well as in various aspects of synaptic plasticity, including synaptotoxicity, synaptic activity and neurotransmission [28].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The miR-132, miR-34a, miR-484, miR-218, miR-455-3p, miR-34a and miR-212 are the potential miRNAs that were studied in mitochondria mediated synaptic functions (Table 1) [29].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For example, miR-132 downregulated in AD and involved in the regulation of PTEN, FOXO3a, P300, NOS1 and MMP- 9 genes thereby enhances neurotransmission and synaptic plasticity [30,31].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: MiR-34a upregulated in AD causes synaptic plasticity dysfunction via the modulation of VAMP2, SYT1, HCN, NR2A and GLUR1 proteins [32].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Another study in 2019, Qian et al., provided evidence that the overexpression of miR-338 in mice is associated with neuropathology in AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The results from in vitro cultured neurons showed an increase in NF-kB activity due to the regulation of miR-338 that might contribute to inflammatory states in patients with AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Analysis of the lysates of hippocampal tissue from 6-month-old 5XFAD transgenic (TG) mice demonstrated that the transcription of miR-338 promoted the expression of BACE1, leading to an increase in Amyloid beta formation resulting in neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction [33].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: Previous studies identified several miRNAs deregulated in AD brain, blood, serum, plasma, CSF and AD mouse model [3,15,16].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: MiRNAs deregulation linked with AD in two ways; (i) the deregulation of miRNAs could be initiated by AD pathogenic factors such as Aβ, p-tau, inflammation, aging, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial DNA damage, and/or (ii) the genetic alteration of miRNAs could be a contributing factor in AD progression.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In both ways, miRNAs significantly contribute to AD via the modulation of expression of disease associated genes/proteins and the regulation of cellular pathways either in a positive or negative way.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Since normal mitochondrial function is crucial to control AD, we recently summarized the potential miRNAs; those are deregulated in AD and involved in several aspects of mitochondrial function such as mitochondrial biogenesis, dynamics, mitophagy, ATP production, oxidative stress and apoptosis, that ultimately lead to impaired synaptic function in AD [3].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Based on the miRNA’s location, association and pivotal roles, we categorized them as ‘mitochondrial localized miRNAs’ and ‘mitochondria associated miRNAs’ (Table 1).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Mitochondria localized miRNAs are supposed to be present and expressed within mitochondria and regulate mitochondrial functions.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: While mitochondria associated miRNAs could be some common miRNAs, those significantly modulate mitochondrial function.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Therefore, several miRNAs are identified in AD, those regulate the key mitochondrial functions; however, it is unclear if these miRNAs are expressed within the mitochondria and transcribed from mitochondrial genome, or what their impact is on the levels of local mitochondrial proteins.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Important mitochondria localized miRNAs and mitochondria-associated miRNAs, their location and their cellular functions in human diseases are summarized in Table 1.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
Aging and Synaptic Dysfunction in Alzheimer’s Disease

Aging is a known factor that increases the progression of brain deterioration, causing epigenetic changes, protein damage and mitochondrial dysfunction, thus contributing to AD progression.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: As an individual begins to age the production of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) is instigated, which alters the electron transport chain.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The result of the disruption to the electron transport chain has been linked to apoptotic cell death.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: According to a research article published in 2021, mutations found in APP, PS1 and PS2 are associated with early onset-AD, whereas age related factors such as ROS production, mitochondrial DNA changes and epigenetic factors have been observed in sporadic AD [8].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Cognitive function depends on synaptic activity and ATP production.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Elderly individuals with AD experience synaptic mitochondria interference through the accumulation of Aβ and p-tau proteins.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The accumulation of these proteins at the nerve terminals and synapses results in defective and inactive mitochondria affecting the communication of neuronal cells.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Recent evidence from postmortem brains of animals and clinical studies suggest that mitochondria play crucial roles in aging and neurodegenerative diseases [8].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Mitochondrial dysfunction was noticed in the postmortem brains of neurodegenerative disease expressing mutant proteins such as Aβ, mutant Htt, mutant SOD1 and mutant DJ1, among others.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Furthermore, the abnormal expression of mitochondrial encoded genes has been observed in AD brains, suggesting that mitochondrial metabolism plays a crucial role in AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

Synapses are crucial for neuronal communication and cognitive function.

source_units.text: Both chemical and electrical synapses compose the complexity of the synaptic network in the human brain.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Chemical synapses receive signals through various presynaptic neurons to a postsynaptic neuron.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Electrical synapses, on the other hand, form connections through gap junctions that result in the direct transfer of ions.

source_units.text: Calcium channels are triggered upon transport of calcium ions into the presynaptic terminal, which releases neurotransmitters through exocytosis.

source_units.text: Mitochondria work to maintain homeostasis by regulating the concentration of calcium depending on ATP consumption.

source_units.text: Summary and Future Directions
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To summarize, miRNAs are involved in cellular changes associated with neurodegenerative diseases and aging.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Alterations in mitochondrial miRNAs expression continue to be an important topic of current research.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Identifying mitochondrial miRNAs changes could help to understand the details of mitochondrial dysfunction in AD progression, could forward the invention of mitochondria based diagnostic tools and could allow the development of suitable preventive strategies against Alzheimer’s disease.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Current studies have suggested that miRNAs significantly contribute to the development and progression of AD in either positive or negative ways.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For this reason, investigating the role of mitochondrial miRNA and understanding their deregulation is necessary to better understand the mitochondrial dysfunction in AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Several key questions are still unanswered in terms of mitochondrial miRNAs and AD pathogenesis: (1) Are mitochondrial genome encoded miRNAs levels altered in AD?
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: (2) If yes, what is the impact of altered mitochondrial miRNA levels on mitochondrial function?
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: (3) Are any mitochondrial miRNAs altered in response to Aβ and p-tau induced toxicities in AD?
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: (4) Is mitochondrial miRNA deregulation responsible for deprived mitochondrial functions and synaptic activity in AD? and (5) What could be the possible miRNAs-based research strategy to improve the mitochondrial function and synaptic activity in AD?
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Therefore, further research is needed to evaluate the critical roles that mitochondrial miRNAs might play in mitochondrial and synaptic function in AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Multi-Omics analysis of brain mitochondria is the best way to understand the genomic and proteomic changes in the mitochondrial genome in AD versus cognitively healthy control brains.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The transcriptomic analysis of brain mitochondrial mRNAs, miRNAs, small RNAs and circular RNAs, and the proteomic analysis of mitochondrial proteins within the same sample, will unveil the local RNA-protein interaction in mitochondria.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The multi-Omics analysis will provide insight into the potential mitochondrial Omics targets altered in the AD brain.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Therefore, a high throughput multi-Omics analysis of the mitochondrial genome and proteome is needed to understand mitochondria-based synaptic dysfunction in AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Further, a deeper understanding of mitochondrial miRNAs could help to develop mitochondrial biomarkers that could be used as a diagnostic tool to detect early stages of AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Further, mitochondrial miRNAs research will help to understand mitochondria-based disease pathobiology and to develop novel therapeutic strategies against AD.
